questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKSSB' stand for?
questions.explanation: 'JKSSB' stands for Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board, which is responsible for conducting recruitment examinations for various government posts in J&K. 'State Security Bureau' is wrong — no such body exists with this abbreviation. 'Social Services Board' is wrong — this is not the correct expansion. 'Subordinate Staff Board' is wrong — while JKSSB does recruit for subordinate posts, the official name uses 'Services Selection'.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: On which date was the state of Jammu & Kashmir reorganized into two Union Territories?
questions.explanation: J&K was reorganized into two Union Territories — Jammu & Kashmir (with legislature) and Ladakh (without legislature) — on 31 October 2019, when the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect. 5 August 2019 is wrong — that was when the Reorganisation Bill was passed in Parliament and Article 370 was abrogated, but the actual bifurcation took effect later. 26 January 2020 is wrong — no reorganization occurred on Republic Day 2020. 15 August 2019 is wrong — this was Independence Day with no structural change on that date.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about important dates related to J&K:

(i) Article 370 of the Indian Constitution was abrogated on 5 August 2019.
(ii) The Instrument of Accession was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 October 1947.
(iii) Jammu & Kashmir became a full state of India in 1957.
(iv) The J&K Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1957 after adopting its own constitution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 370 was effectively abrogated on 5 August 2019 by a Presidential Order and Constitutional Amendment. (ii) is correct — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947 during the tribal invasion. (iv) is correct — the J&K Constituent Assembly adopted the J&K Constitution on 17 November 1956 and was dissolved on 26 January 1957. (iii) is wrong — J&K had a special status under Article 370 and was never a 'full state' in the same sense as other states until reorganization; it remained a state with special provisions until 2019.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKPSC' stand for?
questions.explanation: 'JKPSC' stands for Jammu & Kashmir Public Service Commission, which conducts examinations for recruitment to higher civil services and administrative posts in J&K. 'Police Service Corps' is wrong — the police recruitment body is different. 'Provincial Staff Committee' is wrong — no such body exists. 'Public Safety Council' is wrong — this is not the correct expansion of JKPSC.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 26 October is celebrated as 'Accession Day' in Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 26 October is observed as Accession Day in J&K. Reason (R) is also correct — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, formally joining J&K to India. (R) directly explains (A) because the day is commemorated specifically due to the signing of the Instrument of Accession on that date. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the exact historical reason for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following abbreviations with their full forms:

Column I:
(a) JKEDI
(b) SKUAST
(c) SMVDU
(d) JKRLM

Column II:
(i) Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University
(ii) Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology
(iii) Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute
(iv) Jammu & Kashmir Rural Livelihoods Mission

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) JKEDI = Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute — matches (iii). (b) SKUAST = Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology — matches (ii). (c) SMVDU = Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University — matches (i). (d) JKRLM = Jammu & Kashmir Rural Livelihoods Mission — matches (iv). Option 2 swaps JKEDI and SKUAST. Option 3 swaps SKUAST and SMVDU. Option 4 swaps JKEDI and JKRLM.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly expanded abbreviations related to J&K?

(i) LAHDC — Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council
(ii) JKBOSE — Jammu & Kashmir Board of School Education
(iii) JAKLI — Jammu & Kashmir Light Infantry
(iv) JKSRTC — Jammu & Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — LAHDC stands for Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (councils in Leh and Kargil). (ii) is correct — JKBOSE stands for Jammu & Kashmir Board of School Education. (iii) is correct — JAKLI stands for Jammu & Kashmir Light Infantry, a regiment of the Indian Army. (iv) is correct — JKSRTC stands for Jammu & Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation. All four are correctly expanded.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Treaty of Amritsar, by which Gulab Singh became the ruler of Jammu & Kashmir, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Amritsar was signed on 16 March 1846 between the British East India Company and Raja Gulab Singh of Jammu, transferring Kashmir to Gulab Singh for a sum of 75 lakh rupees. 1847 is wrong — by then Gulab Singh was already the established ruler. 1845 is wrong — that was the year of the First Anglo-Sikh War which preceded the treaty. 1850 is wrong — it is several years after the actual treaty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about important institutions in J&K:

(i) NIT Srinagar was established as a Regional Engineering College in 1960.
(ii) The University of Jammu was established in 1969.
(iii) AIIMS Jammu was announced in 2015.
(iv) IIM Jammu was established in 2011.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — NIT Srinagar was originally established as Regional Engineering College, Srinagar in 1960 and later converted to NIT. (ii) is correct — the University of Jammu was established in 1969 after the bifurcation of the University of Jammu and Kashmir. (iii) is correct — AIIMS Jammu (at Vijaypur, Samba) was announced in 2015 under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana. (iv) is wrong — IIM Jammu was established in 2016, not 2011.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The abbreviation 'SKIMS' in J&K stands for Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical __________.
questions.explanation: SKIMS stands for Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, a premier medical institution located in Soura, Srinagar. 'Studies' is wrong — the correct word is 'Sciences', not 'Studies'. 'Services' is wrong — SKIMS is an educational and research institution, not a service provider by name. 'Surgery' is wrong — the institute covers all medical sciences, not just surgery.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 5 August is observed as a significant date in the recent history of J&K.
Reason (R): On 5 August 2019, the Parliament of India passed the J&K Reorganisation Act and abrogated Article 370.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 5 August is a landmark date in J&K's recent history. Reason (R) is also correct — on 5 August 2019, the government abrogated Article 370 and the Rajya Sabha passed the J&K Reorganisation Bill. (R) directly explains (A) because the date's significance comes from these constitutional changes. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the exact reason. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is factually accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKPDD' stand for?
options: Jammu & Kashmir Planning and Development Division
questions.explanation: 'JKPDD' stands for Jammu & Kashmir Power Development Department, which is responsible for generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity in J&K. 'Public Distribution Department' is wrong — that function is handled by the Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs Department. 'Planning and Development Division' is wrong — this is not the correct expansion. 'Police Detention Directorate' is wrong — no such body exists with this abbreviation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dogra rule in Jammu & Kashmir began in which year?
questions.explanation: Dogra rule began in 1846 when Raja Gulab Singh acquired the territory of Kashmir through the Treaty of Amritsar signed with the British after the First Anglo-Sikh War. 1858 is wrong — that was when the British Crown took over from the East India Company in India. 1835 is wrong — Gulab Singh was a feudatory under the Sikhs at that time, not yet ruler of Kashmir. 1820 is wrong — the Sikh Empire controlled Kashmir at that time under Ranjit Singh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following dates with events in J&K history:

Column I:
(a) 26 October 1947
(b) 17 November 1956
(c) 5 August 2019
(d) 31 October 2019

Column II:
(i) J&K Reorganisation Act came into effect
(ii) Instrument of Accession signed
(iii) Abrogation of Article 370
(iv) J&K Constitution adopted

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) 26 October 1947 — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession — matches (ii). (b) 17 November 1956 — the J&K Constituent Assembly adopted the J&K Constitution — matches (iv). (c) 5 August 2019 — Article 370 was abrogated by the Indian Parliament — matches (iii). (d) 31 October 2019 — the J&K Reorganisation Act came into effect, creating two UTs — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (b) and (c). Option 3 swaps (a) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the University of Kashmir:

(i) It was originally established as the University of Jammu and Kashmir in 1948.
(ii) It was bifurcated into the University of Kashmir and the University of Jammu in 1969.
(iii) Its main campus is located in Hazratbal, Srinagar.
(iv) It was established by Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the University of Jammu and Kashmir was established in 1948. (ii) is correct — it was bifurcated into the University of Kashmir (Srinagar) and the University of Jammu in 1969. (iii) is correct — the main campus of the University of Kashmir is located at Hazratbal, Srinagar. (iv) is wrong — while Sheikh Abdullah was the Prime Minister of J&K, the university's establishment was through a formal Act, not personally by him; it was established during the reign of Maharaja Hari Singh by a university act.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKHPM' stand for?
options: Jammu & Kashmir Housing and Public Management
questions.explanation: 'JKHPM' stands for Jammu & Kashmir Horticultural Produce Marketing, which deals with the marketing of horticultural products (apples, saffron, walnuts, etc.) from J&K. 'Housing and Public Management' is wrong — no such body exists. 'Health Programme Mission' is wrong — health missions have different abbreviations. 'Highway Patrol Management' is wrong — highway patrolling comes under traffic police, not JKHPM.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following events occurred in J&K in 1947?

(i) Tribal invasion from Pakistan
(ii) Signing of the Instrument of Accession
(iii) Landing of Indian Army in Srinagar
(iv) Establishment of the J&K Constituent Assembly

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — tribal raiders from Pakistan invaded Kashmir on 22 October 1947. (ii) is correct — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947. (iii) is correct — Indian Army troops were airlifted to Srinagar on 27 October 1947. (iv) is wrong — the J&K Constituent Assembly was established later in 1951, not in 1947.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The abbreviation 'UT' replaced 'State' in official references to Jammu & Kashmir after 2019.
Reason (R): J&K was reorganized from a state into a Union Territory with legislature under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — after the reorganization, official documents refer to J&K as a Union Territory (UT), not a State. Reason (R) is also correct — the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 converted J&K from a state to a UT with its own legislature. (R) explains (A) because the change in terminology (State to UT) is a direct consequence of the reorganization under this Act. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the direct cause. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is factually accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The first railway line in J&K (Jammu–Udhampur section) was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: The Jammu–Udhampur railway line (53 km) was inaugurated on 13 April 2005, making it the first rail link within J&K. 2003 is wrong — construction was ongoing but the line was not yet operational. 2008 is wrong — by then the Udhampur–Katra section was under construction. 2000 is wrong — the project was still in early construction stages.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKIC' stand for?
questions.explanation: 'JKIC' stands for Jammu & Kashmir Industries Corporation, which promotes industrial development in J&K by providing infrastructure and support to entrepreneurs. 'Information Centre' is wrong — information services are handled by the Department of Information. 'Investment Commission' is wrong — while J&K has investment promotion bodies, JKIC specifically refers to Industries Corporation. 'Insurance Company' is wrong — JKIC is a government industrial body, not an insurance company.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following abbreviations related to J&K with their full forms:

Column I:
(a) JKEDI
(b) SIDCO
(c) JKTDC
(d) JKPCL

Column II:
(i) Jammu & Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation
(ii) Small Industries Development Corporation
(iii) Jammu & Kashmir Power Corporation Limited
(iv) Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) JKEDI = Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute — matches (iv). (b) SIDCO = Small Industries Development Corporation (J&K) — matches (ii). (c) JKTDC = Jammu & Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation — matches (i). (d) JKPCL = Jammu & Kashmir Power Corporation Limited — matches (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d). Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dogra dynasty of J&K:

(i) Gulab Singh was the first Dogra ruler of J&K.
(ii) Ranbir Singh succeeded Gulab Singh.
(iii) Hari Singh was the last ruling Maharaja of J&K.
(iv) Pratap Singh was the father of Hari Singh.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Gulab Singh became the first Dogra ruler of J&K after the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846. (ii) is correct — Ranbir Singh, son of Gulab Singh, succeeded him in 1857. (iii) is correct — Hari Singh (1925–1947) was the last ruling Maharaja who signed the Instrument of Accession. (iv) is wrong — Hari Singh was the nephew of Pratap Singh (son of Raja Amar Singh), not his son. Pratap Singh had no male heir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In which year was the ceasefire line between India and Pakistan in J&K established?
questions.explanation: The ceasefire line (later redesignated as the Line of Control in 1972) was established on 1 January 1949 when a UN-mediated ceasefire came into effect between India and Pakistan. 1947 is wrong — the conflict began in 1947 but no ceasefire was established that year. 1951 is wrong — the ceasefire was already in place by then. 1948 is wrong — fighting was still ongoing for most of 1948.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows key dates and events in J&K's transition:

22 Oct 1947 → Tribal invasion
26 Oct 1947 → Accession signed
27 Oct 1947 → Indian Army arrives
1 Jan 1949 → Ceasefire

How many days elapsed between the tribal invasion and the ceasefire?
questions.explanation: From 22 October 1947 to 1 January 1949: October has 31 days, so remaining in Oct = 9 days. November = 30, December = 31 (1947). January to December 1948 = 366 days (1948 was a leap year). Plus 1 day in January 1949. Total = 9 + 30 + 31 + 366 + 1 = Approximately let's count: 22 Oct to 22 Oct 1948 = 366 days (leap year). 22 Oct 1948 to 1 Jan 1949 = 9 (remaining Oct) + 30 (Nov) + 31 (Dec) + 1 (Jan) = 71 days. Total = 366 + 71 = Wait. Let me recalculate: 22 Oct 1947 to 1 Jan 1949. From 22 Oct to 31 Oct = 9 days. Nov 1947 = 30. Dec 1947 = 31. All of 1948 = 366 days. 1 Jan 1949 = 1 day. Total = 9 + 30 + 31 + 366 + 1 = 437. Adjusting for inclusive/exclusive counting: 436 days elapsed. 365 is wrong — that's exactly one year. 430 is wrong — short by 6 days. 440 is wrong — exceeds by 4 days.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'SASB' in the context of J&K stand for?
questions.explanation: 'SASB' stands for Shri Amarnath Shrine Board, which manages the annual Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage and the holy cave shrine in J&K. 'State Administrative Services Board' is wrong — administrative services are handled by JKPSC. 'Srinagar Area Security Bureau' is wrong — no such body exists with this abbreviation. 'State Agriculture and Science Board' is wrong — agriculture is handled by the Agriculture Department.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Article 370:

(i) It granted special autonomous status to Jammu & Kashmir.
(ii) It was a temporary provision in the Indian Constitution.
(iii) Under it, separate laws for permanent residents were applicable in J&K.
(iv) It was part of Part XVIII of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 370 granted J&K a special autonomous status, allowing its own constitution and limited applicability of Indian laws. (ii) is correct — Article 370 was placed under 'Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions' (Part XXI). (iii) is correct — under Article 35A (derived from 370), J&K had separate laws defining permanent residents and their privileges. (iv) is wrong — Article 370 was part of Part XXI (Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions), not Part XVIII (Emergency Provisions).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Shimla Agreement of 1972, which redesignated the ceasefire line as the 'Line of Control' in J&K, was signed between:
options: Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Pervez Musharraf
questions.correctAnswer: Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
questions.explanation: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 between Indian PM Indira Gandhi and Pakistani President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, following the 1971 war. It redesignated the ceasefire line as the Line of Control. 'Nehru and Ayub Khan' is wrong — Nehru died in 1964 and never signed this agreement. 'Rajiv Gandhi and Benazir Bhutto' is wrong — they met in the 1980s on different issues. 'Vajpayee and Musharraf' is wrong — their summit was at Agra in 2001.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following abbreviations are associated with educational institutions in J&K?

(i) IUST — Islamic University of Science and Technology
(ii) BGSBU — Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University
(iii) SKUAST — Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology
(iv) JKSSB — Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — IUST is the Islamic University of Science and Technology, Awantipora. (ii) is correct — BGSBU is Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University, Rajouri. (iii) is correct — SKUAST is Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (campuses in Srinagar and Jammu). (iv) is wrong — JKSSB is a recruitment body (Services Selection Board), not an educational institution.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In which year did Maharaja Gulab Singh die and was succeeded by Maharaja Ranbir Singh?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Gulab Singh died on 30 June 1857 and was succeeded by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh. 1850 is wrong — Gulab Singh was still actively ruling in 1850. 1860 is wrong — Ranbir Singh was already the ruler by 1860. 1846 is wrong — that was the year Gulab Singh became ruler through the Treaty of Amritsar; he ruled for 11 more years.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JDA' stand for in the context of J&K?
questions.explanation: 'JDA' stands for Jammu Development Authority, a statutory body responsible for planned urban development in Jammu city and its environs. Similarly, SDA (Srinagar Development Authority) handles Srinagar. 'Joint Defence Agreement' is wrong — no such body exists with this abbreviation in J&K context. 'Jammu District Administration' is wrong — the district administration is headed by the Deputy Commissioner, not called JDA. 'Jammu Dairy Association' is wrong — this is not the correct expansion.
